claim: The study included an accelerated longitudinal cohort of 234 adolescents and young adults scanned at two time points.
source: We studied an accelerated longitudinal cohort of adolescents and young adults (n = 234, two time points) to investigate dynamic reconfigurations in myeloarchitecture.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract with specific sample size and design details.

claim: Intracortical profiles were generated using magnetization transfer (MT) data, a myelin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging contrast.
source: Intracortical profiles were generated using magnetization transfer (MT) data, a myelin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging contrast.
evidence: Directly stated methodology in the abstract.

claim: Mixed-effect models demonstrated two separate developmental processes: overall increases in MT and flattening of the MT profile related to enhanced signal in mid-to-deeper layers.
source: Mixed-effect models of depth specific intracortical profiles demonstrated two separate processes i) overall increases in MT, and ii) flattening of the MT profile related to enhanced signal in mid-to-deeper layers, especially in heteromodal and unimodal association cortices.
evidence: Primary finding stated in abstract based on statistical modeling.

claim: MT profile changes especially affected heteromodal and unimodal association cortices.
source: Mixed-effect models of depth specific intracortical profiles demonstrated two separate processes i) overall increases in MT, and ii) flattening of the MT profile related to enhanced signal in mid-to-deeper layers, especially in heteromodal and unimodal association cortices.
evidence: Spatial specificity of findings stated in abstract.

claim: MT profile development was independent of morphological changes.
source: This development was independent of morphological changes.
evidence: Stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: Enhanced MT in mid-to-deeper layers spatially co-localized with gene expression markers of oligodendrocytes.
source: Enhanced MT in mid-to-deeper layers was found to spatially co-localise specifically with gene expression markers of oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Finding from gene expression analysis stated in abstract.

claim: Intracortical changes contributed to a gradual differentiation of higher-order from lower-order systems.
source: Interregional covariance analysis revealed that these intracortical changes contributed to a gradual differentiation of higher-order from lower-order systems.
evidence: Finding from covariance analysis stated in abstract.

claim: Adolescence is a crucial phase in biological and psychosocial maturation involving large-scale reconfigurations of brain anatomy.
source: Adolescence is a crucial phase in biological and psychosocial maturation and involves large-scale reconfigurations of brain anatomy (Paus et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Previous studies have shown marked age-related changes in brain structure during adolescence.
source: Previous histopathological and neuroimaging studies have shown marked age-related changes in brain structure during this sensitive period (Giedd et al., 2015; Raznahan et al., 2011; Sowell et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: MRI assessments have revealed regionally-variable dynamics of cortical thinning in adolescence.
source: This is particularly evident in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessments of the macro-structural morphology of cortical regions, which have revealed regionally-variable dynamics of cortical thinning in adolescence (Giedd et al., 2015; Raznahan et al., 2011; Sowell et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior MRI studies.

claim: Morphometric analyses typically only quantify shape changes of the inner and outer cortical boundaries.
source: While these findings confirm the existence of strong biological forces shaping adolescent brain anatomy, morphometric analyses typically only quantify shape changes of the inner and outer cortical boundaries.
evidence: Statement about limitations of existing methods based on established knowledge.

claim: Morphometric analyses may not be specific for microstructural changes occurring within the cortical mantle.
source: In turn, these analyses may not be specific for microstructural changes occurring within the cortical mantle, which ultimately play key roles in adolescent development of cortical connectivity and function (Huntenburg et al., 2017).
evidence: Inference about limitations supported by citation.

claim: Magnetisation transfer (MT) is an MRI acquisition sequence sensitive to how water molecules interact with macromolecules in the brain, notably myelin.
source: One promising imaging technique is magnetisation transfer (MT), an MRI acquisition sequence that is sensitive to how water molecules interact with macromolecules in the brain, notably myelin (Schmierer et al., 2007).
evidence: Technical description supported by citation.

claim: MT cannot be equated with cortical myelin content per se.
source: Although techniques such as MT cannot be equated with cortical myelin content per se (Serres et al., 2009a; Serres et al., 2009b), the MT parameter is dominated by myelin-related molecules making this technique a viable in vivo proxy for the contrast seen histologically in myelin basic protein (Koenig, 1991; Odrobina et al., 2005; Whitaker et al., 2016).
evidence: Limitation acknowledged with citations.

claim: The MT parameter is dominated by myelin-related molecules making it a viable in vivo proxy for myelin basic protein.
source: Although techniques such as MT cannot be equated with cortical myelin content per se (Serres et al., 2009a; Serres et al., 2009b), the MT parameter is dominated by myelin-related molecules making this technique a viable in vivo proxy for the contrast seen histologically in myelin basic protein (Koenig, 1991; Odrobina et al., 2005; Whitaker et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: A post mortem study in multiple sclerosis patients showed that MT measures scale with demyelination and remyelination.
source: A post mortem study in patients with multiple sclerosis has also shown that MT measures scale with demyelination and remyelination, suggesting dependence of this measure on myelin content (Schmierer et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to specific study.

claim: MT is arguably the strongest in vivo marker of myelin based on its spatial correspondence with myelin basic protein.
source: While correlated with alternative myelin-sensitive imaging, MT is arguably the strongest in vivo marker of myelin, based on its spatial correspondence with myelin basic protein (Whitaker et al., 2016).
evidence: Comparative claim supported by citation.

claim: Recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers.
source: While recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers (Carey et al., 2018; Grydeland et al., 2019; Kwon et al., 2018; Whitaker et al., 2016), findings have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claim: Previous myelin-marker studies have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
source: While recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers (Carey et al., 2018; Grydeland et al., 2019; Kwon et al., 2018; Whitaker et al., 2016), findings have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
evidence: Limitation of prior work stated with citations.

claim: Previous studies have generally focused on specific depths or intracortical averages, ignoring depth-dependent dynamics.
source: Furthermore, studies have generally focused on specific depths or intracortical averages, ignoring depth-dependent dynamics and thus not addressing potential systematic shifts in cortical myeloarchitecture and lamination in adolescence.
evidence: Critique of prior literature based on review.

claim: Quantitative profiling of intracortical properties using central moments has been proposed to characterise cytoarchitecture in seminal histological work.
source: Quantitative profiling of intracortical properties across cortical depths, and specifically parameterization using central moments (Papoulis and Unnikrishna Pillai, 2002), has been proposed to characterise cytoarchitecture in seminal histological work (Schleicher et al., 1999) and capture inter-individual variation (Amunts et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to methodological papers.

claim: The mean (first moment) of MT profiles allows inferences on overall myelin content.
source: In essence, studying the mean (first moment) of MT profiles perpendicular to the cortical mantle allows inferences on overall myelin content while higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes (Figure 1).
evidence: Methodological interpretation with figure reference.

claim: Higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes in MT profiles.
source: In essence, studying the mean (first moment) of MT profiles perpendicular to the cortical mantle allows inferences on overall myelin content while higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes (Figure 1).
evidence: Methodological interpretation with figure reference.

claim: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers.
source: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers, and depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity (Zilles et al., 2002) and cortical hierarchy (Mesulam, 1998).
evidence: Methodological interpretation supported by citations.

claim: Depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity and cortical hierarchy.
source: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers, and depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity (Zilles et al., 2002) and cortical hierarchy (Mesulam, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Classical histological findings showed overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence.
source: Applied to adolescence, such an analysis offers a non-invasive window into cortical architecture, which may recapitulate and expand classical histological findings showing overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence (Kaes, 1907) as well as transcriptional analyses suggesting that laminar signatures reflect cortical development (Miller et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to classical work.

claim: Transcriptional analyses suggest that laminar signatures reflect cortical development.
source: Applied to adolescence, such an analysis offers a non-invasive window into cortical architecture, which may recapitulate and expand classical histological findings showing overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence (Kaes, 1907) as well as transcriptional analyses suggesting that laminar signatures reflect cortical development (Miller et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation.

claim: Microstructure profile covariance (MPC) quantifies inter-regional similarity in microstructure at a single subject-level.
source: One such approach, known as microstructure profile covariance (MPC), quantifies inter-regional similarity in microstructure at a single subject-level (Paquola et al., 2019).
evidence: Methodological description supported by citation.

claim: MPC has demonstrated utility for understanding large-scale patterns of cortical architecture, illustrating a sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation.
source: Previous research has demonstrated the utility of MPC for understanding large-scale patterns of cortical architecture, specifically illustrating a sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation in both post mortem and in vivo datasets (Paquola et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The sensory-fugal gradient describes gradual transitions from primary sensory and motor regions with high laminar differentiation through association cortex toward paralimbic areas with increasingly dysgranular appearance.
source: This axis describes gradual transitions from primary sensory and motor regions with high laminar differentiation, through association cortex toward paralimbic areas with increasingly dysgranular appearance (Mesulam, 1998).
evidence: Description supported by citation.

claim: Microstructural similarity predicts cortico-cortical connectivity.
source: Given prior evidence that microstructural similarity predicts cortico-cortical connectivity (Barbas and Rempel-Clower, 1997), tracking age-related changes in MPC provides an unprecedented way to probe coordinated maturation of microstructural networks during the critical adolescent period, moving towards a network perspective of structural brain development (Alexander-Bloch et al., 2013; Váša et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation.

claim: The cortex-wide average MT profile shows a non-linear increase in intensity from superficial layers towards deeper layers.
source: At baseline (i.e., using the average across timepoint 1), the cortex-wide average MT profile shows a non-linear increase in intensity from the superficial layers, adjacent to the pial boundary, towards the deeper layers approaching the white matter boundary, consistent with prior literature (Whitaker et al., 2016; Figure 1A).
evidence: Baseline finding supported by citation and figure.

claim: MT profiles show similar variations in mean and skewness across levels of laminar differentiation as post mortem myelin stained sections.
source: Although post mortem myelin stained sections and in vivo MT profiles differ in terms of resolution and specificity to myelin, we observed similar variations in mean and skewness of profiles across levels of laminar differentiation (Figure 1B), supporting the extension of profile analysis from histology to in vivo MT imaging.
evidence: Comparison finding with figure reference.

claim: Mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation.
source: At a whole cortex-level, mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation, while skewness exhibited an opposite pattern (spatial correlation = −0.23, pspin <0.001; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: Baseline finding with statistical support and figure references.

claim: Skewness exhibited an opposite pattern to mean MT across levels of laminar differentiation.
source: At a whole cortex-level, mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation, while skewness exhibited an opposite pattern (spatial correlation = −0.23, pspin <0.001; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: Baseline finding with statistical support and figure references.

claim: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths.
source: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths, whereas more positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers (Zilles et al., 2002; Figure 1C).
evidence: Baseline finding with citation and figure reference.

claim: More positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers.
source: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths, whereas more positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers (Zilles et al., 2002; Figure 1C).
evidence: Baseline finding with citation and figure reference.

claim: The first principal gradient of MPC was anchored on one end by idiotypic sensory regions and by paralimbic regions on the other end.
source: In line with previous work (Paquola et al., 2019), the first principal gradient within the baseline cohort was anchored on one end by idiotypic sensory regions and by paralimbic regions on the other end.
evidence: Baseline finding supported by citation.

claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001).
source: This sensory-fugal gradient reflects systematic variations in the MT profiles; it was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001; Figure 1D) and weakly with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
evidence: Statistical finding with figure reference.

claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was weakly correlated with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
source: This sensory-fugal gradient reflects systematic variations in the MT profiles; it was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001; Figure 1D) and weakly with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
evidence: Statistical finding with figure reference.

claim: Adolescence led to a significant increase in mean MT (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [4.8 14.7] 95% CIs).
source: Studying age-related changes in MT moments, we observed that adolescence led to a significant increase in the mean (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [4.8 14.7] 95% CIs; Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting overall increases in intracortical myelin content.
evidence: Primary longitudinal finding with statistical support and figure references.

claim: Adolescence led to decreases in skewness (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [−179.2–34.6] 95% CIs).
source: Conversely, we observed a unique spatial pattern of decreases in skewness (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [−179.2–34.6] 95% CIs; Figure 2).
evidence: Primary longitudinal finding with statistical support and figure reference.

claim: Decreases in skewness reflected preferential increases in MT in mid to deeper layers.
source: Depth-wise changes in MT intensity suggest that these decreases in skewness reflected a preferential increases in MT in mid to deeper layers, suggesting accumulation in myelin.
evidence: Interpretation of depth-wise data.

claim: Controlling for overall mean MT trajectories resulted in virtually identical patterns of skewness change.
source: Controlling for overall mean MT trajectories resulted in virtually identical patterns of skewness change, suggesting relative independence between skewness and mean MT trajectories in adolescence (Appendix 1—figures 2–4).
evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claim: Age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024).
source: Across all moments, age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024), while idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented than expected by chance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Statistical finding with figure and supplementary file references.

claim: Idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented in age-related skewness changes than expected by chance.
source: Across all moments, age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024), while idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented than expected by chance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Statistical finding with figure and supplementary file references.

claim: The spatial distribution of MT profile mean and skewness were virtually unchanged when controlled for morphological and intensity confounds (r > 0.99).
source: To this end, we computed residual MT moments by controlling for thickness or interface blurring at each vertex within node-wise linear models. The spatial distribution of MT profile mean and skewness were virtually unchanged when data were additionally controlled for morphological and intensity confounds (r > 0.99; Appendix 1—figures 2–4).
evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claim: Age-related changes in MT moments were virtually identical when using MT profile data corrected for cortical thickness and interface blurring (r > 0.98).
source: Age-related changes in MT moments were also virtually identical when using MT profile data corrected for cortical thickness and interface blurring (r > 0.98, Appendix 1—figures 2–4), supporting that MT profile trajectories were primarily driven by intracortical factors.
evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claim: MT moments were relatively independent of regional variations in laminar thickness derived from post mortem volumetric reconstruction (mean: −0.06 < r < 0.05. skewness: −0.17 < r < 0.02).
source: Furthermore, spatial correlations suggested that MT moments were relatively independent of regional variations in laminar thickness derived from a post mortem volumetric reconstruction of a Merker-stained human brain (Wagstyl et al., 2018) (mean: −0.06 < r < 0.05. skewness: −0.17 < r < 0.02; Appendix 1—figure 5).
evidence: Comparison analysis with citation and figure reference.

claim: The pattern of age-related change in skewness showed enrichment exclusively with oligodendrocytes (p<0.001 at a specificity index threshold of 0.0001).
source: Cell specific expression analysis (Dougherty et al., 2010) suggested enrichment exclusively with oligodendrocytes (p<0.001 [at a specificity index threshold of 0.0001]; Figure 3A), confirming the association between myelination and decreased MT skewness.
evidence: Gene expression analysis finding with citation and figure reference.

claim: Developmental expression analysis showed selective enrichment for adolescence and young adulthood.
source: Developmental expression analysis (Dougherty et al., 2010) showed selective enrichment for adolescence and young adulthood (Figure 3B).
evidence: Gene expression analysis finding with citation and figure reference.

claim: Gene ontology analysis indicated a negative association with demyelination (Z = −2.16, p=0.001) and axon degeneration (Z = −2.34, p=0.011).
source: Furthermore, we performed gene ontology analysis using a modified Fishers exact test, which captures the deviation from the expected gene rank (Kuleshov et al., 2016), on genes associated with decreasing skewness. This indicated a negative association with demyelination (Z = −2.16, p=0.001) and axon degeneration (Z = −2.34, p=0.011), reinforcing associations to myelin.
evidence: Gene ontology analysis finding with citation.

claim: Genes negatively associated with age-related skewness reduction were less likely to be enriched for demyelination and were exclusively associated with oligodendrocytes.
source: In sum, genes negatively associated with age-related skewness reduction were less likely to be enriched for demyelination and were exclusively associated with oligodendrocytes.
evidence: Summary of gene expression findings.

claim: MT skewness changes during adolescent development appear to be strongly reflective of changes in myelination.
source: Thus, MT skewness changes during adolescent development appear to be strongly reflective of changes in myelination.
evidence: Interpretation based on gene expression analyses.

claim: Exploratory rank-based correlations indicated a small correlation between mean and skewness related genes (rho = 0.14, p<0.001).
source: However, exploratory rank-based correlations on the weights of each gene indicated a small correlation between mean and skewness related genes (rho = 0.14, p<0.001), indicating mean and skewness share a modest transcriptomic signature.
evidence: Statistical finding from gene expression analysis.

claim: Baseline data analysis did not identify a whole genome transcriptional profile that overlapped with any of the baseline MT moments.
source: Finally, it should be noted that the same analysis on baseline data only (average across a single scan per subject) from this cohort did not identify a whole genome transcriptional profile that overlapped with any of the baseline MT moments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), reinforcing the added value of developmental data (e.g. measuring an age-related change) in detecting human neurodevelopmental processes by myelin-sensitive MRI.
evidence: Negative finding with figure reference.

claim: At the edge-level, adolescent development was primarily related to increases in MPC (1564 increases vs 534 decreases at qFDR <0.025).
source: At the node-to-node edge-level, adolescent development was primarily related to increases in MPC (1564 increases vs 534 decreases at qFDR <0.025; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: MPC analysis finding with figure reference.

claim: The first principal component (G1DEV) illustrated a sensory-fugal gradient, explaining 33% variance.
source: The first principal component (G1DEV) illustrated a sensory-fugal gradient, explaining 33% variance (Figure 4A).
evidence: Dimensionality reduction finding with figure reference.

claim: Idiotypic sensory and motor areas became increasingly coupled in adolescence, and more segregated from paralimbic nodes.
source: On one end of the gradient, idiotypic sensory and motor areas became increasingly coupled in adolescence, and more segregated from the opposite anchor constituted mainly of paralimbic nodes.
evidence: Interpretation of gradient analysis.

claim: The concordance of the developmental gradient (G1DEV) with the baseline MPC gradient (r = 0.89, p<0.001) suggested that the axis of microstructural differentiation expands during adolescence.
source: The concordance of the developmental gradient (G1DEV) with the baseline MPC gradient (r = 0.89, p<0.001, Figure 1D) suggested that the axis of microstructural differentiation expands during adolescence.
evidence: Statistical finding with interpretation and figure reference.

claim: Heteromodal and unimodal cortex were drawn outwards towards one of the gradient anchors in older individuals.
source: Heteromodal and unimodal cortex, occupying central regions of the gradient, were drawn outwards towards one of the gradient anchors in older individuals (Figure 4B), forming a more bimodal distribution (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure references.

claim: Prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas in older individuals.
source: Specifically, prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas, and temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions (Figure 4B).
evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure reference.

claim: Temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions in older individuals.
source: Specifically, prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas, and temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions (Figure 4B).
evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure reference.

claim: Greater decreases in MT skewness were related to sensory anchor coupling (r = −0.63, pspin <0.001).
source: By relating the age-related shifts in MPC to anchors with age-related changes in MT moments, we found that greater decreases in MT skewness were related to sensory anchor coupling (r = −0.63, pspin <0.001; Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Correlation finding with figure references.

claim: Restricted age-related skewness changes were associated with paralimbic anchor coupling (r = 0.65, pspin <0.001).
source: Conversely, restricted age-related skewness changes were associated with paralimbic anchor coupling (r = 0.65, pspin <0.001).
evidence: Correlation finding.

claim: Depth-dependent myelination during adolescence reshapes myeloarchitecture and underpins macro-scale reorganisation of cortical networks.
source: Together, these findings demonstrate how depth-dependent myelination during adolescence reshapes myeloarchitecture and underpins macro-scale reorganisation of cortical networks.
evidence: Summary interpretation of findings.

claim: Adolescent development was characterized by two developmental processes: one involving overall increases in mean MT and one involving preferential MT increases in mid-to-deeper cortical layers.
source: Changes to intracortical myelin can be generally characterised by two developmental processes, one involving overall increases in mean MT and one involving preferential MT increases in mid-to-deeper cortical layers.
evidence: Summary of primary findings.

claim: Both developmental processes particularly affected unimodal and heteromodal association cortices.
source: Both processes particularly affected unimodal and heteromodal association cortices that is areas between low-level sensory and motor areas on the one end of the cortical hierarchy and high-level transmodal and limbic regions on the other end.
evidence: Summary of spatial findings.

claim: Intracortical microstructural changes were independent from age-related effects on overall cortical morphology and tissue contrast.
source: A series of complementary explorations, based on alternative neuroimaging features known to undergo large-scale changes in adolescence (Giedd et al., 2015; Raznahan et al., 2011; Sowell et al., 2004), demonstrated the independence of these intracortical microstructural changes from age-related effects on overall cortical morphology and tissue contrast.
evidence: Summary of control analyses with citations.

claim: Patterns of age-related change overlapped with genes associated with oligodendrocyte processes.
source: In addition, cross-referencing our findings against post mortem gene expression maps showed that patterns of age-related change overlapped with genes associated with oligodendrocyte processes, supporting the specificity of MT changes to myelin.
evidence: Summary of gene expression findings.

claim: Local processes were paralleled by a cortex-wide differentiation along the sensory-fugal axis.
source: Leveraging microstructure profile covariance analysis, we explored coordination of intracortical microstructure characteristics across distributed areas (Paquola et al., 2019). This showed that local processes were paralleled by a cortex-wide differentiation along the sensory-fugal axis.
evidence: Summary of MPC findings with citation.

claim: The sensory-fugal axis underpins the segregation of lower- from higher-order components of the putative cortical hierarchy.
source: This axis ultimately underpins the segregation of lower- from higher-order components of the putative cortical hierarchy.
evidence: Interpretation of gradient findings.

claim: The skewness of the MT profile tilts from infragranular-dominant in paralimbic regions towards a more even distribution across cortical depths in sensory regions.
source: The skewness of the MT profile, reflecting nonlinear increases in myelin towards deeper layers (Dinse et al., 2015; Sprooten et al., 2019; Waehnert et al., 2014), tilts from infragranular-dominant in paralimbic regions towards a more even distribution across cortical depths in sensory regions.
evidence: Interpretation of baseline findings with citations.

claim: The graded shift in skewness parallels changes in the laminar origin of projections.
source: This graded shift parallels changes in the laminar origin of projections, where paralimbic regions engaged in feedback processing project from infragranular layers and sensory regions providing feedforward information project predominantly from supragranular layers (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991).
evidence: Interpretation linking findings to known connectivity patterns with citation.

claim: Mean myelin increased from polar towards sensory regions, recapitulating prior post mortem evidence and established atlases of cytoarchitecture.
source: Meanwhile, mean myelin increased from polar towards sensory regions, recapitulating prior post mortem evidence (Vogt and Vogt, 1919; Vogt, 1911), established atlases of cytoarchitecture (Von Economo and Koskinas, 2008), and resting-state functional connectivity gradients (Hong et al., 2017; Margulies et al., 2016).
evidence: Baseline finding supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mean and skewness trajectories showed concomitant but independent developmental patterns.
source: Tracking longitudinal change in intracortical MT profiles, we found concomitant but independent developmental patterns in the trajectory of mean and skewness.
evidence: Summary of longitudinal findings.

claim: Both mean and skewness changes were strongly and preferentially located in heteromodal and unimodal association cortex, yet they only partially overlapped.
source: Both sets of age-related changes were strongly and preferentially located in heteromodal and unimodal association cortex; yet, they only partially overlapped, a finding also supported by gene expression analysis.
evidence: Summary of spatial and gene expression findings.

claim: Only skewness changes, but not mean MT changes, were spatially associated with oligodendrocyte gene expression patterns.
source: Only skewness changes, but not mean MT changes, were spatially associated with oligodendrocyte gene expression patterns.
evidence: Gene expression finding.

claim: Skewness effects occurred independently of MRI-based measures of cortical interface blurring and variations in cortical thickness.
source: Additional analyses indicated that skewness effects occurred rather independently of MRI-based measures of cortical interface blurring and variations in cortical thickness, supporting specificity to intracortical microstructure.
evidence: Summary of control analyses.

claim: Increasing mean MT likely reflects myelination of previously unmyelinated axons.
source: Our findings may align with several mechanisms of experience-dependent myelination (de Faria et al., 2018). Increasing mean MT likely reflects myelination of previously unmyelinated axons.
evidence: Interpretation with citation.

claim: Skewness changes likely capture architectural reconfigurations or laminar specific changes in axonal myelination.
source: On the other hand, as skewness changes persisted even after controlling for changes in the mean, these more likely capture architectural reconfigurations or laminar specific changes in axonal myelination.
evidence: Interpretation based on control analyses.

claim: Underlying mechanisms may include de novo generation of oligodendrocytes, activity-dependent modifications in neuronal and oligodendrocyte precursors, and tuning of the distance between nodes of Ranvier.
source: Underlying mechanisms may include de novo generation of oligodendrocytes (Zuccaro and Arlotta, 2013), activity-dependent modifications in neuronal and oligodendrocyte precursors (Gibson et al., 2014), and tuning of the distance between nodes of Ranvier along both cortico-cortical as well as long-range axons (Arancibia-Cárcamo et al., 2017).
evidence: Speculation about mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: The putative functional role of myelin in cortical grey matter may be to insulate fibres from making new synaptic connections, thus enhancing stability.
source: The putative functional role of myelin in cortical grey matter may be to insulate fibres from making new synaptic connections, thus enhancing stability (Braitenberg, 1962; Braitenberg and Schüz, 1998; Micheva et al., 2016).
evidence: Speculation about function supported by citations.

claim: Overall lower myelin content in transmodal regions might indicate a higher potential for plasticity.
source: Conversely, overall lower myelin content in transmodal regions might indicate a higher potential for plasticity (Huntenburg et al., 2017), possibly making these areas more suitable to support adaptive behaviour and learning that are core to many integrative functions that mature during adolescence.
evidence: Speculation supported by citation.

claim: Rodent experiments suggest that experience-induced oligodendrocyte remodelling supports the development of positive social behaviour.
source: Rodent experiments suggest that experience-induced oligodendrocyte remodelling supports the development of positive social behaviour (Makinodan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to animal studies.

claim: Abnormal myelination has been implicated in several brain disorders.
source: Conversely, abnormal myelination has been implicated in several brain disorders, however, studies on intracortical myeloarchitecture are scarce (Mighdoll et al., 2015; Stedehouder and Kushner, 2017; Bernhardt et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations.

claim: The architectural changes observed may represent a microstructural substrate that could determine overall cognitive and social capacities or susceptibility to neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions.
source: The architectural changes observed in the present cohort may represent a microstructural substrate that could determine overall cognitive and social capacities or susceptibility to a range of neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions occurring in late childhood and adolescence.
evidence: Speculation about implications.

claim: Decreases in MT profile skewness pushed regions to a more sensory-like architecture.
source: Specifically, decreases in MT profile skewness pushed regions to a more sensory-like architecture (which was coupled with high mean MT).
evidence: Interpretation of MPC findings.

claim: Increases in skewness pushed regions towards a paralimbic-like MT profile.
source: In contrast, increases in skewness pushed regions towards a paralimbic-like MT profile.
evidence: Interpretation of MPC findings.

claim: Two regionally distinct developmental patterns within the association cortex promoted a more bimodal distribution of myeloarchitectural types across the cortex.
source: These two regionally distinct developmental patterns within the association cortex promoted a more bimodal distribution of myeloarchitectural types across the cortex.
evidence: Summary interpretation of findings.

claim: Similar properties of modular segregation in tractography-based networks have been shown to mediate age-related improvements in executive function throughout adolescence.
source: Similar properties of modular segregation in tractography-based networks have been shown to mediate age-related improvements in executive function throughout adolescence (Baum et al., 2017), reinforcing the importance of these processes for understanding psychosocial maturation.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Drifts in association cortex towards either sensory-like or paralimbic-like architecture represents an expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation.
source: Drifts in association cortex towards either sensory-like or paralimbic-like architecture represents, thus, an expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation (Paquola et al., 2019).
evidence: Interpretation with citation.

claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was previously described by Mesulam based on non-human primate research to encapsulate cortex-wide variations in architecture and connectivity.
source: Such a sensory-fugal gradient was previously described by Mesulam (1998) based on non-human primate research to encapsulate cortex-wide variations in architecture and connectivity, and has since been suggested to reflect increasing synaptic plasticity towards transmodal regions (García-Cabezas et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations.

claim: Systematic variations in the degree of experience-dependent plasticity may explain why myelin-derived markers develop differently along the sensory-fugal gradient.
source: Systematic variations in the degree of experience-dependent plasticity may explain why myelin-derived markers develop differently along the sensory-fugal gradient (de Faria et al., 2018), in contrast to other known developmental gradients such as the rostro-caudal timing of terminal neurogenesis (Rakic, 1974).
evidence: Speculation supported by citations.

claim: Differentiation of association cortices conforms with notions of the 'tethering hypothesis' of cortical evolution.
source: Differentiation of association cortices also conforms with notions of the 'tethering hypothesis' of cortical evolution (Buckner and Krienen, 2013).
evidence: Interpretation supported by citation.

claim: According to the tethering hypothesis, intermediate regions of the cortical hierarchy are less constrained by extrinsic inputs and intrinsic signaling molecules, which has allowed for massive surface area expansion throughout mammalian evolution.
source: According to this framework, intermediate regions of the cortical hierarchy are less constrained by extrinsic inputs and intrinsic signaling molecules, which has allowed for massive surface area expansion throughout mammalian evolution.
evidence: Description of cited framework.

claim: Reduced constraints on association cortices allow for protracted development of myeloarchitecture, whereas the sensory and limbic anchors are well-defined prior to adolescence.
source: Our findings suggest that reduced constraints on association cortices allow for protracted development of myeloarchitecture, whereas the sensory and limbic anchors are well-defined prior to adolescence.
evidence: Interpretation of findings in context of tethering hypothesis.

claim: The NSPN study comprises a primary cohort of 2402 healthy young people recruited from schools, colleges, NHS primary care services and direct advertisements in north London and Cambridgeshire.
source: In brief, the NSPN study comprises a primary cohort of 2402 healthy young people, recruited from schools, colleges, NHS primary care services and direct advertisements in north London and Cambridgeshire.
evidence: Description of cohort.

claim: Participants were stratified into five age groups (14–15, 16–17, 18–19, 20–21 and 22–25 years) and each stratum was evenly balanced for sex and ethnicity.
source: Participants were stratified into five age groups (14–15, 16–17, 18–19, 20–21 and 22–25 years) and each stratum was evenly balanced for sex and ethnicity.
evidence: Description of study design.

claim: The secondary cohort sub-sampled approximately 60 individuals from each stratum in the primary cohort, maintaining the sex and ethnicity balance.
source: The secondary cohort sub-sampled approximately 60 individuals from each stratum in the primary cohort, maintaining the sex and ethnicity balance.
evidence: Description of study design.

claim: Cohort retention for the MRI follow-up was 74%.
source: Cohort retention for the MRI follow-up was 74% (Kiddle et al., 2018).
evidence: Retention statistic with citation.

claim: Following quality control, the final sample included 180 individuals (age stratification at baseline, n = 39/41/39/33/26, inter-scan interval = 15.4 ± 3.5 months, 86 females).
source: Further inclusion criteria for the present study were availability of T1w and MT data available at two timepoints, resulting in 234 healthy adolescents. Following additional quality control on raw images, surface reconstructions and MT profiles, detailed below, the sample included 180 individuals (age stratification at baseline, n = 39/41/39/33/26, inter-scan interval = 15.4 ± 3.5 months, 86 females).
evidence: Final sample characteristics after quality control.

claim: T1w and MT imaging were acquired as part of the quantitative multiparameter mapping (MPM) sequence on three identical TIM Trio 3T scanners.
source: T1w and MT imaging were acquired as part of the quantitative multiparameter mapping (MPM) sequence (Weiskopf et al., 2013) on three identical TIM Trio 3T scanners; two located in Cambridge and one located in London.
evidence: Acquisition details with citation.

claim: The MT saturation parameter decouples the MT signal from the longitudinal relaxation rate, making it a semi-quantitative measure that is robust to relaxation times and field inhomogeneities.
source: The MT saturation parameter decouples the MT signal from the longitudinal relaxation rate, making it a semi-quantitative measure that is robust to relaxation times and field inhomogeneities (Weiskopf et al., 2013; Hagiwara et al., 2018).
evidence: Technical description supported by citations.

claim: Equivolumetric intracortical surfaces better coincide with the position of the putative cortical laminae than equidistant or Laplace-field guided techniques.
source: Our vertex-wise technique leverages equivolumetric transformations that critically adjust surface placement in accordance to the folded cortical sheet (Wagstyl et al., 2018), thereby better coinciding with the position of the putative cortical laminae than equidistant or Laplace-field guided techniques (Waehnert et al., 2014).
evidence: Methodological comparison supported by citations.

claim: The intracortical approach offered better precision and biological validity over conventional voxel-based morphometry techniques.
source: Our intracortical approach thus offered better precision and biological validity over conventional voxel-based morphometry techniques that may be agnostic to cortical topology and intracortical architecture, and that may amplify mixing of different tissue types (Ziegler et al., 2019).
evidence: Methodological comparison with citation.
